title: Archive or unarchive a want on direct request
summary: Set one want inactive or restore it to active without changing its captured content, propagating state to Annals, or retaining transition history.
use_when: The user directly requests archival or unarchival of one identified captured want.
do_not_use_when: Completion, inactivity or decision associations merely suggest a lifecycle change.
The request concerns deleting or editing source content, freezing Annals associations, or changing decision records.
outcome: The selected want has the requested durable local state and remains readable under the same identity.
effects: Sets or removes only the selected want's current archive marker in private Conatus settings.
Runs no Annals command, model, email send, or scheduler operation.
authority: The user directly chooses the transition. Conatus owns lifecycle state; Annals owns independent source interpretation and associations.
success: The local transaction commits and returns changed plus record with the resulting state. A repeated transition succeeds with changed:false.
failure_and_recovery: Unknown IDs, decision IDs, maintenance holds and storage errors fail without a successful transition receipt. Inspect want show ID after uncertain command completion; repeating the same transition is safe.
privacy: State remains private and local. No archival reason, timestamp, actor or transition history is stored. Ordinary metadata-only command usage observation remains separate.
does_not_authorize: Automatic or inferred lifecycle transitions, source edits, deletion, Annals mutation, publication or sending email.

consumers.statement: The local user or an agent acting on the user's direct archive or unarchive request selects one want.

preconditions.statement: Conatus state is initialized and writable, the ID identifies a captured want, and product maintenance admission is open. Annals need not be available.

inputs.statement: want archive WANT_ID or want unarchive WANT_ID selects one exact existing want. Global --state-dir ABS_PATH selects private local state.

outputs.statement: JSON {ok:true,data:{changed,record}} returns the saved record and whether state changed. Errors use {ok:false,error:string}. record.state is active or archived.

data_semantics.statement: Archived means inactive, not completed. Captured identity, wording, source, capture time and outgoing document stay unchanged. Only unarchive changes an archived want's lifecycle. Processing receipts and Annals associations remain independent.

identity_and_units.statement: The existing want-UUIDv7 identity is preserved. No archival timestamps or units are introduced.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: The receipt describes one selected want at the local transaction commit. New and existing wants without an archive marker are active. No archival history is retained.

access.statement: Current-user local CLI operations require a direct user request for each transition. Background processing and models do not infer archive or unarchive actions.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: A transaction changes only the current archive marker. Repeated commands are no-ops. State never propagates to Annals, other records, frozen documents or frozen email occurrences. Active lists and newly rendered emails omit archived wants.

operational_limits.statement: One exact want is selected per command. No bulk or automatic lifecycle operation is provided.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Existing schema-one settings hold current archive markers. Absence means active, so no migration is required. Older releases ignore markers and can show or email archived wants.

reliances.statement: The transition uses Conatus local storage and admission only; it invokes no external product or service.
